content:
Apple TV has long been hailed as the "new HBO," known for prioritising quality over quantity. But in recent months the streaming platform has been ramping up its roster of shows so aggressively that there's simply too much to keep up with.

Apple TV steps into a new era, with quality and quantity rising in tandem

I've been subscribed to Apple TV since its launch in 2019, and there are usually only one or two shows on the platform at any given time that I actually want to watch.

This production model is very similar to HBO's — HBO built its brand by producing a smaller number of shows that were generally of a higher calibre, beating most of its competitors in the process.

Over the past few years, however, Apple has gradually increased its output while at the same time appearing to raise the bar in terms of quality.

The result is that Apple now has so many great shows on the go that I genuinely can't keep up.

The following are the series currently releasing new episodes on Apple TV every week:

  • Ted Lasso — one of my personal favourites
  • Slow Horses — another all-time great in Apple's catalogue
  • Dark Matter — a sci-fi series whose first season I absolutely loved, but whose second season I haven't started yet
  • Brothers — a new half-hour comedy starring Matthew McConaughey and Woody Harrelson that looks pretty fun
  • Last Seen — a new thriller I've heard good things about but haven't watched
  • There's also Women in Blue and Knife Edge Edge, which I might get to during a less busy season, but for now they're further down my list

I really want to start Dark Matter, because the first season elevated it to one of my favourite sci-fi shows of all time, just behind Severance and Pluribus. But it's genuinely hard to find the time to begin season two. And half-hour comedies have always been my go-to comfort viewing, so Brothers is already lined up next.

I enjoy crime thrillers and shows about family, so Last Seen looks right up my alley. Even with Stephen King's endorsement, though, I still haven't started it.

And that's only what's currently airing.

Silo — I haven't finished season 3 yet, and Sugar season 2 I haven't even opened, despite the glowing reviews and my own love of the show. If I ignored every other streaming platform, I could obviously watch a lot more on Apple, but the shows on other services are also eating up a significant chunk of my time.

October is fast approaching, and Apple is about to drop seven brand-new series and films all at once — the most I can recall in a single month.

All in all, I'm genuinely thrilled at how well Apple TV is doing right now. Apple beating HBO to take home more Emmys this year was no fluke.

What are your thoughts on Apple TV's recent and current slate of shows? Share them with us in the comments below.

Apple TV costs $14.99 per month, with a discount available when bundled through Apple One.
